newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks bounce back as Dow rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks bounce back as Dow rebounds.

text.p: The Australian share market headed higher at the open on Tuesday with a rebound on Wall Street providing enough motivation to ensure a firmer tone.
However, much of the local focus was on profits with newspaper publishers John Fairfax and Australian Provincial Newspapers, serum maker CSL and Capral Aluminium all due to report during the day.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 23.4 points to 2,641.9.

"New York was up last night and we have bounced back a bit even if the volumes are nothing to speak of so far," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage, adding that near term business was likely to be a little choppy.
"We are in the thick of the results at the moment so that may push things around a little."
In broader terms, the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve later on Monday would be watched with interest although policy was expected to remain unchanged.
Among the leaders Rio Tinto and WMC failed to share in the bounce as weaker metals prices pressured miners. Rio shares lost eight cents to A$20.90 (US$15.45), while WMC lost one to A$7.27.

Fellow miner and bellwether BHP found support in its role as market leader, adding 17.2 cents to A$17.28. Among industrials, media giant News Corp was steady at A$5.92 ahead of its full year results due early on Wednesday Sydney time.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of over six to one, while about 25 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
